desc: A sibling reject-row narrowing a decimal-backed business-domain field with `>=` produces a conservative SUPERSET narrowing in the next row (e.g. `>= '10.0 each'` rejected is treated as `<= '9.0 each'`, not the precise `< '10.0 each'`) — the proof engine under-claims on decimal boundaries rather than accepting unsoundly.
exercise:
field Counter as quantity in 'each'
from S on E1
  when Counter >= '10.0 each'
    -> reject 'too many'
from S on E2
  -> set Counter = Counter + '9.5 each'

desc: A Tier 3 UCUM atom — grammar-valid but not in the Tier 1 (~150) or Tier 2 (~500) discovery lists surfaced in completions — is structurally accepted as a `quantity` unit; the full UCUM grammar admits any well-formed expression regardless of discovery tier.
exercise: field Viscosity as quantity in 'St'

desc: A bare UCUM time-unit abbreviation (not inside a compound denominator) used as a `quantity` unit is rejected — time units are excluded from UCUM's domain in Precept and belong exclusively to `period`/`duration`.
exercise: field Elapsed as quantity in 'h'

desc: A number-literal bound (not a typed constant) on a qualifier-bearing field, including a negative literal, is extracted unchanged for interval-containment proof — bound extraction is exact and never rounds.
exercise: field Adjustment as quantity in 'kg' min -100

desc: A unit name absent from any standard registry (UCUM or the curated counting-unit set) is accepted when declared via a `unitofmeasure` field default and referenced as an entity-scoped unit inside a compound `quantity in` constraint — entity-scoped units are recognized from field declarations, not a separate registry.
exercise:
field PackUnit as unitofmeasure default 'six-pack'
field StockPerPack as quantity in 'each/{PackUnit}'

desc: No dedicated `units { }` declaration block construct exists in the language (D6's rejected alternative) — using this proposed-but-never-adopted syntax is a parse/compile error.
exercise: units { case, pack, pallet }

desc: Guard-narrowing an open `period` field's `.basis` to an exact single-unit set discharges a downstream time-denominator cancellation obligation requiring that same unit (D14 subset match: the narrowed non-zero component set is a subset of what the operation requires).
exercise:
field Gap as period
field HourlyRate as price in 'USD/hours'
field Pay as money in 'USD'
from Active on Calc
  when Gap.basis == 'hours'
    set Pay = HourlyRate * Gap

desc: Guard-narrowing an open `period` field's `.basis` to a composite set that is not a subset match for the required single-unit denominator does not discharge the obligation — a composite-basis period cannot cancel a single-unit price denominator (CompoundPeriodDenominator).
exercise:
field Gap as period
field HourlyRate as price in 'USD/hours'
field Pay as money in 'USD'
from Active on Calc
  when Gap.basis == 'hours + minutes'
    set Pay = HourlyRate * Gap

desc: A `set` reassignment of an open `period` field after a `.dimension`/`.basis` narrowing guard invalidates the narrowing fact — a downstream obligation later in the same action chain does not discharge against the stale fact.
exercise:
field Gap as period
field OtherGap as period
field DueDate as date
from Active on Extend
  when Gap.dimension == 'date'
    set Gap = OtherGap
    set DueDate = DueDate + Gap

desc: `.basis` accessor on a single-basis `in`-constrained `period` field returns the canonical basis name as a string.
exercise:
field Gap as period in 'hours'
field B as string
from S on E
  -> set B = Gap.basis

desc: `.basis` accessor on a composite-basis period returns the canonical coarse-to-fine spaced form regardless of the order components were declared in (`'minutes + hours'` declared, `'hours + minutes'` returned).
exercise:
field Gap as period in 'minutes + hours'
field B as string
from S on E
  -> set B = Gap.basis

desc: `.basis` accessor on an open (unconstrained) `period` field returns the runtime decomposition — the canonical string of every non-zero component at access time, with zero-valued components omitted.
exercise:
field Gap as period
field B as string
from S on E
  -> set B = Gap.basis

desc: `.dimension` accessor on a date-only-basis `period` (e.g. `in 'days'`) returns `'date'`.
exercise:
field Gap as period in 'days'
field D as dimension
from S on E
  -> set D = Gap.dimension

desc: `.dimension` accessor on a time-only-basis `period` (e.g. `in 'hours'`) returns `'time'`.
exercise:
field Gap as period in 'hours'
field D as dimension
from S on E
  -> set D = Gap.dimension

desc: `.dimension` accessor on a period spanning both date and time components (e.g. `in 'days + hours'`) returns `'datetime'` — a return-only dimension value, not a declarable `of` constraint.
exercise:
field Gap as period in 'days + hours'
field D as dimension
from S on E
  -> set D = Gap.dimension

desc: Guard-narrowing an open `period` field's `.dimension` to `'date'` proves it safe for `date ± period` arithmetic (the doc's own worked example).
exercise:
field Interval as period
field DueDate as date
from Active on Extend
  when Interval.dimension == 'date'
    set DueDate = DueDate + Interval
  else
    reject "Extension interval must use date components"

desc: An open `period` field used in `date ± period` arithmetic without a `.dimension` narrowing guard is a compile error — the field's temporal dimension is unproven.
exercise:
field Interval as period
field DueDate as date
from Active on Extend
  -> set DueDate = DueDate + Interval

desc: `date - date` assigned to a `period` field with no `in` constraint uses NodaTime's default basis (Years, Months, Days) rather than requiring an explicit basis declaration.
exercise:
field StartDate as date
field EndDate as date
field Gap as period
from S on E
  -> set Gap = EndDate - StartDate

desc: A composite period basis with more than one atom illegal for the source operation emits one diagnostic per violating atom (e.g. `date - date` assigned to `period in 'hours + minutes'` — both `hours` and `minutes` are time atoms illegal for a date-only subtraction).
exercise:
field StartDate as date
field EndDate as date
field Gap as period in 'hours + minutes'
from S on E
  -> set Gap = EndDate - StartDate

desc: `precept_update` money value with exactly one space between magnitude and ISO 4217 code is accepted at the Door 2 deserialization boundary.
exercise:
field Amount as money in 'USD'
# precept_update { "Amount": "100.00 USD" }

desc: `precept_update` money value missing the required single space between magnitude and currency code violates the Door 2 parse contract.
exercise:
field Amount as money in 'USD'
# precept_update { "Amount": "100.00USD" }

desc: `precept_update` price value with whitespace around the `/` separator violates the "no space around /" parse contract for compound currency/unit ratios at the Door 2 boundary.
exercise:
field Rate as price in 'USD/each'
# precept_update { "Rate": "4.17 USD / each" }

desc: An unrecognized ISO 4217 code in an `exchangerate` value at the `precept_update` boundary is treated as a parse failure (diagnostic), never a thrown exception.
exercise:
field FxRate as exchangerate in 'USD/EUR'
# precept_update { "FxRate": "1.08 USD/FAKE" }

desc: decimal must be exact base-10 arithmetic — 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 holds exactly (doc's explicit worked claim); no float drift. Runtime-value assertion, not just a compile-accept.

desc: number is IEEE 754 double — 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3 (doc's explicit worked claim). The rule compiles (line 83: 'proof engine cannot prove exact equality on number', so it is not statically rejected); the drift is a runtime-observable value, which Phase 2 must check against the doc's claim rather than treat as a bare compile-accept.
exercise: field A as number default 0.1; field B as number default 0.2; rule A + B == 0.3 because "number is approximate"

desc: floor(NaN) is a documented runtime fault ('NaN is not a number'). NaN cannot arise via literal syntax or via a statically-provable path; it must enter through an unconstrained event-arg number value, since the compiler cannot prove finiteness of external input and (per line 658) is not required to reject it at compile time — the fault is runtime-defensive.
exercise:
event SetScore(V as number)
on SetScore -> set N = floor(SetScore.V)

desc: ceil(NaN) is a documented runtime fault, same reasoning as the floor case.

desc: Every declared constraint with proof semantics produces an obligation on every applicable mutation path (Obligation Generation Contract) — a minlength field's assignment is checked.
exercise: field X as string minlength 3; field Src as string; on E -> set X = Src

desc: A maxcount-declared collection produces a count-containment obligation on every growing mutation (Obligation Generation Contract).
exercise: field C as set of string maxcount 10; field V as string; on E -> add C V

desc: When the compiler cannot prove a computed value stays inside its declared limit it rejects the definition rather than deferring to a runtime check (prove-or-reject MVP).
exercise: field A as integer; field Capped as integer min 0 max 100 <- A

desc: When an obligation cannot be discharged the compiler rejects AND names what would make the operation provably safe (remediation guidance in the diagnostic).
exercise: field Divisor as integer; on E -> set R = Total / Divisor   // diagnostic should name the guard/modifier that discharges

desc: A bound requiring transitive combination of two separate facts (allocations<=commitments + commitments<=plan) is out of scope — single-hop only — so it stays unproven and rejects.
exercise: field Alloc as integer; field Commit as integer; field Plan as integer; rule R1: Alloc <= Commit because "..."; rule R2: Commit <= Plan because "..."; on E -> set R = Plan / (Plan - Alloc)

desc: General dataflow across transitions is out of scope — a value made safe only by a prior transition's action is not tracked, so a dependent fault-prone op in a later transition rejects.
exercise: state A initial; state B; on Setup from A to B -> set X = 5; on Use from B -> set R = Total / X

desc: An obligation whose site contains a type-error operand emits NO proof diagnostic (root cause already reported upstream; no cascading proof diagnostic).
exercise: field Divisor as integer; on E -> set R = Total / (Divisor + undefinedName)

desc: A transition originating from an unreachable state has its proof obligations vacuously satisfied (the transition can never fire) — no proof diagnostic from that row.
exercise: state A initial; state Orphan; state B; on E from Orphan to B -> set R = Total / 0

desc: The proof engine runs for stateless precepts — a fault-prone op in an event handler still rejects when unproven.
exercise: field Divisor as integer; on Compute -> set R = Total / Divisor   // stateless, no states
